title: Ezekiel Chapter 4 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Ezekiel chapter 4 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Ezekiel Chapter 4 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Ezekiel Chapter 4.

questions.question: In Ezekiel 4, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Take a tile and portray Jerusalem
Set an iron pan as a wall
questions.correctAnswer: Take a tile and portray Jerusalem
questions.explanation: This action is described first in the chapter, specifically in Ezekiel 4:1.

questions.question: What city is Ezekiel instructed to portray on the tile?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is commanded to portray the city, even Jerusalem, as stated in Ezekiel 4:1.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel lay against the city?
questions.explanation: He is instructed to build a fort against the city as mentioned in Ezekiel 4:2.

questions.question: What shall Ezekiel set around the city?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is told to set battering rams against the city, as stated in Ezekiel 4:2.

questions.question: What is to be placed as a wall of iron between Ezekiel and the city?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is instructed to take an iron pan and set it for a wall of iron, according to Ezekiel 4:3.

questions.question: For how many days is Ezekiel to lie on his left side?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is told that he shall bear their iniquity for 390 days, as stated in Ezekiel 4:5.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel bear on his left side?
options: The iniquity of the house of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: The iniquity of the house of Israel
questions.explanation: He is to lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon his left side, according to Ezekiel 4:4.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel do after lying on his left side?
options: He lies on his right side
questions.correctAnswer: He lies on his right side
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is instructed to lie again on his right side after accomplishing the days, as stated in Ezekiel 4:6.

questions.question: How many days is Ezekiel to bear the iniquity of the house of Judah?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel shall bear the iniquity of the house of Judah for 40 days, as mentioned in Ezekiel 4:6.

questions.question: How many years of iniquity has God laid upon Ezekiel?
questions.explanation: God has laid upon Ezekiel the years of their iniquity for 390 days, according to Ezekiel 4:5.

questions.question: This shall be a sign to which house?
questions.explanation: This besieging is a sign to the house of Israel as stated in Ezekiel 4:3.

questions.question: Is Ezekiel instructed to set battering rams against the city?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is indeed instructed to set battering rams against the city as per Ezekiel 4:2.

questions.question: Does Ezekiel lay upon his right side for 390 days?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel lays on his left side for 390 days and then on his right side for 40 days, as stated in Ezekiel 4:5 and 4:6.

questions.question: Ezekiel is commanded to portray the city of Babylon.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel is commanded to portray the city of Jerusalem, not Babylon, as stated in Ezekiel 4:1.

questions.question: Ezekiel bears the iniquity of the house of Israel for 40 days.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel bears the iniquity of the house of Israel for 390 days, not 40 days, as stated in Ezekiel 4:5.

medium.title: Ezekiel Chapter 4 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Ezekiel Chapter 4 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What will Ezekiel do against Jerusalem according to Ezekiel 4:7?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:7 states, 'Therefore thou shalt set thy face toward the siege of Jerusalem, and thine arm shall be uncovered, and thou shalt prophesy against it,' indicating that Ezekiel is commanded to prophesy.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 4:8 promise will happen if someone lays siege against Jerusalem as commanded in Ezekiel 4:7?
options: They will not turn from side to side
questions.correctAnswer: They will not turn from side to side
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:8 states, 'And, behold, I will lay bands upon thee, and thou shalt not turn thee from one side to another, till thou hast ended the days of thy siege,' indicating a commitment to the siege.

questions.question: What ingredients does Ezekiel use to make bread according to Ezekiel 4:9?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:9 lists 'wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentiles, and millet, and fitches' as the ingredients to make bread, highlighting the specific items required.

questions.question: What is the significance of lying on the left side according to Ezekiel 4:4?
options: It is a sign of victory
It symbolizes the iniquity of Israel
It represents a time of rest
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the iniquity of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:4 states, 'Lie thou also upon thy left side, and lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it,' indicating that this act symbolizes bearing their iniquity.

questions.question: How much meat is Ezekiel instructed to eat daily according to Ezekiel 4:10?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:10 specifies that 'thy meat which thou shalt eat shall be by weight, twenty shekels a day,' indicating the exact amount for daily sustenance.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel use for baking according to Ezekiel 4:12?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:12 states, 'thou shalt eat it as barley cakes, and thou shalt bake it with dung that cometh out of man,' indicating the unconventional method of preparation.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel's 390 days of lying on his side symbolize according to Ezekiel 4:5?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:5 specifies, 'For I have laid upon thee the years of their iniquity,' indicating that the duration symbolizes the iniquity of Israel.

questions.question: What does Ezekiel 4:6 instruct him to do after the 390 days?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:6 states, 'And when thou hast accomplished them, lie again on thy right side,' indicating a further act of bearing iniquity.

questions.question: How is the water Ezekiel drinks described in Ezekiel 4:11?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:11 specifies, 'Thou shalt drink also water by measure,' indicating a controlled and limited intake.

questions.question: What does the iron pan represent in Ezekiel 4:3?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:3 states, 'Moreover take thou unto thee an iron pan, and set it for a wall of iron between thee and the city,' indicating a division or barrier.

questions.question: What is the overall purpose of the actions Ezekiel is commanded to perform in chapter 4?
questions.explanation: The entire chapter serves as a prophetic sign to the house of Israel regarding the impending judgment and siege, as indicated by the actions commanded.

questions.question: Lying on his side for an extended period teaches us about the importance of what in our spiritual lives?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's long duration of lying on his side teaches about the importance of enduring hardship with faithfulness and patience.

questions.question: Is it true that Ezekiel was instructed to eat bread baked with dung?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:12 clearly states that he was to bake his bread with dung, signifying the severity of the situation.

questions.question: Is it true that Ezekiel was allowed to turn from side to side during his siege?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:8 indicates that he would not turn from one side to another until the days of his siege were completed.

questions.question: Is it true that Ezekiel's actions were a sign to the house of Israel?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's actions were indeed a sign to the house of Israel, as stated in Ezekiel 4:3, indicating the prophetic nature of his actions.

hard.title: Ezekiel Chapter 4 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Ezekiel Chapter 4.

questions.question: What did the LORD say the children of Israel would eat among the Gentiles?
questions.explanation: The LORD said, 'Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.' (Ezekiel 4:13)

questions.question: What was Ezekiel's response to the LORD regarding his eating habits?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel said, 'Ah Lord GOD! behold, my soul hath not been polluted...' (Ezekiel 4:14)

questions.question: What did the LORD give Ezekiel to use instead of man's dung?
questions.explanation: The LORD said, 'Lo, I have given thee cow's dung for man's dung...' (Ezekiel 4:15)

questions.question: How did the people in Jerusalem need to eat bread according to Ezekiel 4:16?
questions.explanation: The LORD said, '...and they shall eat bread by weight, and with care...' (Ezekiel 4:16)

questions.question: What will the people experience as a result of their iniquity according to Ezekiel 4:17?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'That they may want bread and water, and be astonied one with another...' (Ezekiel 4:17)

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'defiled' in Ezekiel 4:13 mean?
questions.explanation: The word 'defiled' refers to something that is contaminated or made unclean, aligning with the context of the bread they would eat.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used in Ezekiel 4:16?
questions.explanation: The breaking of the 'staff of bread' symbolizes the coming scarcity and judgment upon Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects with the theme of eating defiled bread as mentioned in Ezekiel 4:13?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 65:4 speaks about those who eat swine's flesh and broth of abominable things, reflecting a similar theme of defilement.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of hunger and scarcity as prophesied in Ezekiel 4:16?
questions.explanation: Amos 8:11 speaks of a famine of hearing the words of the LORD, which connects to the scarcity mentioned in Ezekiel.

questions.question: What comes before Ezekiel 4:15?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:14 precedes 4:15, where he expresses his concern about being polluted.

questions.question: What comes after Ezekiel 4:17?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:1 follows 4:17, as the next chapter begins with further instructions to Ezekiel.

questions.question: The act of lying upon one side to bear iniquity reflects which cultural practice?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's actions symbolize the burden of Israel's iniquity, which is a common prophetic action in biblical literature.

questions.question: The phrase 'staff of bread' in Ezekiel 4:16 indicates what about the state of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The 'staff of bread' symbolizes the sustenance that will be judged and broken due to the people's sin.

questions.question: The statement 'Even thus shall the children of Israel eat' implies which aspect of their condition?
questions.explanation: This statement indicates the dire condition the Israelites will face in exile, as they will eat defiled bread (Ezekiel 4:13).

questions.question: Ezekiel's dietary restrictions were a sign of God's favor upon him.
questions.explanation: Ezekiel's restrictions reflect the judgment upon Israel, not favor, as he was to act out the consequences of their iniquity (Ezekiel 4:14).

theological.title: Ezekiel Chapter 4 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Ezekiel Chapter 4 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 4:4 teach about human sin?
options: The corporate nature of Israel's iniquity is borne by a prophetic representative
Human sin is only individual and never corporate
Sin is forgiven without bearing any consequences
Prophets are exempt from bearing the iniquities of the people
questions.correctAnswer: The corporate nature of Israel's iniquity is borne by a prophetic representative
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:4 shows the prophet lying on his side to bear the iniquity of the house of Israel, indicating a representative bearing of corporate sin.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 4:6 teach about the relationship between Israel and Judah?
options: Both Israel and Judah share culpability but are distinct entities in judgment
Israel and Judah are identical in their covenant identity
Only Judah bears sin and Israel is innocent
Judah will be spared while Israel alone is punished
questions.correctAnswer: Both Israel and Judah share culpability but are distinct entities in judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:6 differentiates between Israel and Judah by assigning different symbolic days to bear their iniquity, showing distinct but shared culpability.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's prophetic signs is taught in Ezekiel 4:8?
options: God uses symbolic actions that prophets must faithfully perform to communicate judgment
Prophetic signs are optional and symbolic only for private reflection
God no longer uses physical signs but only spoken word
Prophets may choose which signs to obey based on personal preference
questions.correctAnswer: God uses symbolic actions that prophets must faithfully perform to communicate judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:8 commands the prophet to remain bound and not turn until the days are ended, demonstrating the necessity of faithful symbolic action.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 4:13 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:13 reveals God's just judgment as the children of Israel are made to eat defiled bread among the Gentiles because of their sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Ezekiel 4:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:17 describes the people consuming away for their iniquity, showing God's wrath as a response to persistent sin.

questions.question: How does the symbolic siege and famine in Ezekiel 4 prepare for themes fulfilled in the book of Jeremiah?
options: It prefigures the actual Babylonian siege and exile prophesied in Jeremiah
It contradicts Jeremiah’s message of immediate restoration
It replaces Jeremiah’s prophecies about destruction with hope only
It teaches that exile was avoidable through sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the actual Babylonian siege and exile prophesied in Jeremiah
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4’s siege symbolism foreshadows the historical Babylonian siege that Jeremiah also prophesies, linking judgment themes across the prophetic corpus.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is made in Ezekiel 4:16 regarding God's judgment?
options: God’s breaking of the staff of bread anticipates the judgment leading to Israel’s exile and eventual restoration
It symbolizes permanent destruction without hope
It denies any future restoration promise for Israel
It reflects only a natural famine with no spiritual significance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s breaking of the staff of bread anticipates the judgment leading to Israel’s exile and eventual restoration
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:16 uses the breaking of the staff of bread as a symbol of impending famine and siege, which historically culminated in exile but sets the stage for future restoration.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 4:4 and 4:5 teach about sin and atonement?
options: The corporate bearing of sin involves a divinely appointed period of suffering representing years of iniquity
Sin is only individual and has no corporate consequences
The prophet’s suffering is unrelated to Israel’s sin
Atonement is immediate without prolonged bearing of iniquity
questions.correctAnswer: The corporate bearing of sin involves a divinely appointed period of suffering representing years of iniquity
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 show Ezekiel bearing Israel’s iniquity for 390 days, each day symbolizing a year, teaching corporate guilt and atonement through suffering.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 4:9 and 4:10 teach about divine judgment and provision?
options: Judgment entails scarcity and measured provision, emphasizing God's sovereign control over sustenance
God abandons the people entirely without any provision
Judgment is only spiritual and not physical
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment entails scarcity and measured provision, emphasizing God's sovereign control over sustenance
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:9-10 describe measured food portions during judgment, showing God’s sovereign regulation of physical sustenance as part of divine discipline.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Ezekiel 4:12 and 4:15 teach about the severity of judgment and the prophet's obedience?
options: Prophetic obedience includes enduring shame and impurity to demonstrate the severity of Israel’s defilement
The prophet refuses to endure defilement and is excused
Judgment is only symbolic and involves no real defilement
God protects the prophet from any physical hardship
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic obedience includes enduring shame and impurity to demonstrate the severity of Israel’s defilement
questions.explanation: Verses 12 and 15 show Ezekiel baking bread using human dung (changed to cow dung) symbolizing the defilement Israel experiences; the prophet submits obediently.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Ezekiel 4:9-11 teaches that God endorses unclean food and water consumption. What does Ezekiel 4:9-11 actually teach?
options: God uses unclean food and limited water symbolically to represent judgment and scarcity, not endorsement of impurity
God commands unclean eating as a permanent law for Israel
The passage teaches that unclean food is spiritually beneficial
God’s provision is unlimited and pure during judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God uses unclean food and limited water symbolically to represent judgment and scarcity, not endorsement of impurity
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:9-11 uses unclean food and scant water as symbolic acts portraying the severity of judgment, not as divine approval of impurity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Ezekiel 4:2 teach about God's sovereignty over nations?
options: God sovereignly directs the siege and judgment against Jerusalem through foreign powers
God is powerless to stop foreign sieges
Nations act independently without divine control
Judgment is arbitrary and not connected to divine will
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly directs the siege and judgment against Jerusalem through foreign powers
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:2’s imagery of siege and fortifications points to God’s sovereign orchestration of geopolitical events for judgment.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Ezekiel 4:3 regarding God’s protection and judgment?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:3 depicts an iron wall between the prophet and the city, symbolizing God’s sovereign control in both protecting and judging Israel.

questions.question: How does Ezekiel 4:14 contribute to the theological understanding of prophetic obedience and human purity?
options: It shows the prophet's concern for ritual purity and personal holiness within judgment
It denies the need for prophetic obedience in judgment
It teaches that prophets can ignore personal purity
It suggests prophets are exempt from God’s commands
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the prophet's concern for ritual purity and personal holiness within judgment
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:14 reveals the prophet’s distress over defiling his soul, highlighting the importance of prophetic personal holiness amid judgment.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine about divine discipline and human responsibility is taught in Ezekiel 4:16 and 4:17?
options: God’s discipline leads to physical suffering that results from human iniquity and calls for repentance
Suffering is random and unrelated to sin
God’s discipline removes all human responsibility
Physical suffering is only natural with no theological meaning
questions.correctAnswer: God’s discipline leads to physical suffering that results from human iniquity and calls for repentance
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 4:16-17 link the breaking of bread and scarcity of water to consequences of iniquity, teaching divine discipline conditioned by human sin.
